questions.question: 1. Selection sort is an unstable sorting algorithm.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Selection sort can be implemented as a stable sorting algorithm if swaps are done carefully to preserve the order of equal elements.
explanations.b: Correct. While the standard implementation may not be stable, selection sort can be made stable by avoiding unnecessary swaps.

questions.question: 2. What is the worst-case time complexity for the selection sort algorithm?

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(N) is too fast for selection sort, which requires nested iterations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(NLogN) is typical for more efficient algorithms like merge sort or quick sort.
explanations.c: Correct. Selection sort has O(N^2) worst-case time complexity due to two nested loops.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(N^3) would require three nested loops, which selection sort does not have.
